entries: Materials and preparation | Transporting and unloading and organizing | Driving mobile equipment to transport materials and parts to the excavation site, using hand tools to unload materials and devices and mechanical parts, and organizing materials for use.

Equipment installation and adjustment | Installation and adjustment and disassembly | Installing and adjusting equipment used to excavate geological materials, and assisting in the disassembly and assembly of extraction and drilling and boring equipment.

Operation observation and monitoring | Observing equipment operation and reporting anomalies | Observing and monitoring equipment operation during extraction to detect anomalies and reporting them to craft workers.

Assisting extraction operations | Assisting craft workers and collecting samples and signaling | Providing assistance to earth drillers and derrick operators and mining machine operators, collecting and checking geological samples, and signaling the start of extraction or drilling.
Cleaning and tidying | Cleaning the site and preparing the site | Cleaning the site and removing debris after work, and cleaning and preparing the excavation or drilling site.

Safety and collaboration | Blasting and machinery and site safety | Working with craft workers and crews according to blasting and explosives and work permit and machinery and height and edge and dust and contaminant requirements, and handling anomalies and reporting.

paragraphs: Site and environment | Open-pit mines and oil and gas sites and underground operations are the main workplaces; the work schedule changes with weather and production and contract periods (60% irregular) (O*NET work context and task scope, same below) → Protection and exposure | Exposure to hazardous equipment is common (89% every day); exposure to contaminants is common (81% every day); exposure to machinery and blasting and drilling noise is common; exposure to machinery and hand tool vibration → Physical stamina and posture | Long periods of standing and standing more than half the time (61% more than half the time); often working in narrow or elevated spaces and in open-pit or underground operations; high physical proximity (34% very close, 60% within arm's length) → Communication and collaboration | Close collaboration with craft workers and colleagues (72% continuous contact with others); frequent face-to-face discussions (88% every day) → Precision and responsibility | Relatively high precision and coordination requirements (45% extremely important); relatively serious consequences of error (56% extremely serious, 12% very serious); relatively high responsibility for others' health and safety (65% extremely high responsibility) → Progress and pace | Constrained by production plans and process interfaces; production interfaces and schedules bring time pressure (31% every day); the pace is determined by craft workers and production progress → Decision making and equipment | High decision frequency (68% every day); equipment and machinery and drilling tools and hand tools → Scheduling and site | Schedules are mostly irregular, changing with weather and production (60% irregular, 38% regular); work is mainly team-based; the work schedule changes with weather and production and contract periods (60% irregular) → Digitalization | Relatively little use of email and mobile communication; equipment monitoring and maintenance records and project communication applications

Records and collaboration notes | Start from the work task sheet and site conditions, first checking the site and working face, equipment and machinery and drilling tools, materials and spare parts, key points for observing and monitoring equipment operation, excavation and loading and handling, cleaning and site tidying before and after work, and signals and communication and work permits, then assist with the work according to craft worker and production requirements and hand over by shift. Matters involving blasting and explosives and machinery and height and edges must be carried out according to qualifications and policy, and traceable equipment and work records must be retained.

BLS wage scope presented by O*NET | This page corresponds to O*NET/SOC 47-5081.00 (Helpers--Extraction Workers). It must be stated faithfully: the 2025 U.S. wages presented by O*NET on the 47-5081.00 page are a median hourly wage of $22.95 / median annual wage of $47,730 (2025, BLS OEWS, this occupation's (47-5081.00) own scope); in the distribution, the 10th percentile is an hourly wage of $17.77 and an annual wage of $36,960, the 25th percentile is an hourly wage of $19.92 and an annual wage of $41,430, the 75th percentile is an hourly wage of $27.84 and an annual wage of $57,920, and the 90th percentile is an hourly wage of $32.70 and an annual wage of $68,020, all taken from the BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS 2025, as presented by O*NET); that page does not mark the data as taken from a parent or adjacent occupation, so it is presented according to this occupation's (47-5081.00) own scope; production incentive bonuses are included, benefits, overtime, and non-production bonuses are excluded, and the median is not an entry-level starting wage. Mainland China has not established a national occupational wage distribution precisely corresponding to this occupation, and this page registers the gap according to the evidence policy rather than filling it in.
Receive records → Verify source IDs → Check shift records → Retain discrepancies → Name the reviewer → Hand off

Mainland China scope and gaps | Mainland China has positions in mining and oil and gas and drilling and geological engineering similar to Helpers--Extraction Workers (such as extraction helper, drilling worker assistant, mine auxiliary worker, and earthwork worker), and their work and blasting and drilling and machinery and height and edges and loading and unloading and safety and occupational health and records are governed by the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and related regulations and standards on civil explosives and special operations and occupational health and environmental protection. However, the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages of urban unit employees by industry category and does not distinguish occupations, and public occupational statistics have not established a national occupational wage distribution precisely corresponding to O*NET 47-5081.00 (Helpers--Extraction Workers); this page retains the search scope and the gap, and does not infer starting pay, take-home income, or personal quotations from industry averages, recruitment offers, or U.S. data.

Safety and compliance notes | Organize work according to work safety and blasting and explosives and machinery and height and edge and dust and contaminant and occupational health and record requirements: observation and monitoring and handling and installation and tidying and cleaning must be consistent with work procedures and current standards and must indicate sources and limitations, and must not replace blasting work permits, equipment safety inspection, or safety permit requirements; operations involving blasting and explosives and height and edges and machinery and loading and unloading must be handled with work permits and personal protection as required; the collection and use and external provision of enterprise and site and equipment manufacturer technical materials must have a lawful basis, be limited to the minimum necessary scope, and be approved and documented according to policy.

The precise BLS 47-5081 projection for 2025—2035 is about 7,100 → 7,200 people, growth 1.7%, average annual openings 700 including replacements, and self-employment in the base period 5.5%; this is not real-time hiring, net growth, or AI causality.

Accepting the task and checking the site → Equipment and machinery inspection → Material and spare part transport and organizing → Equipment installation and adjustment → Observing and monitoring operation and assisting extraction → Cleaning and preparing the site and records and handover

Standards and quality boundaries | This page involves three types of requirements: first, technical and quality — observation and monitoring and handling and installation and tidying and cleaning must be performed according to work procedures and current standards with equipment and work records kept; second, safety and occupational health — blasting and explosives and machinery and height and edge and dust and contaminants and personal protection must meet work safety and special operations and occupational health requirements; third, environment and ecology — the disposal of dust and noise and wastewater and waste and site restoration must meet environmental protection and soil and water conservation requirements; all three are governed by the currently effective version and the requirements of the competent authority and the enterprise.

Records and collaboration | According to the enterprise's production and quality and safety management systems, record task sheets, equipment and machinery and observation and monitoring, materials and usage, installation and adjustment and assisting extraction, cleaning and tidying and anomalies and rework and outstanding items and shift handover and original records and revision trail, and check the site and equipment with craft workers and crews and equipment and safety personnel; anomalies must be isolated and reported promptly.

Boundary conclusion | This page corresponds to O*NET 47-5081.00 (Helpers--Extraction Workers), and the core difference from adjacent positions lies in "subject matter and outputs and authorization level": this occupation takes extraction equipment and machinery and the site and on-site coordination as its subject matter, produces assisted work completed according to work procedures (materials and observation and monitoring and installation and adjustment and tidying and cleaning) together with traceable equipment and work records, completes work within the scope of craft worker and job authorization based on equipment and site and coordination ability, and is responsible for work safety and production order; earth drillers and derrick operators and mining machine operators and blasters produce their own professional work, with different responsibility and authorization levels.

Core concept of adjacent positions | Most positions in the same group and adjacent positions aim to "complete extraction or drilling or blasting or loading and unloading work to the specified quality within work procedure and safety requirements and keep records", with differences in subject matter and outputs and authorization level: some take independent drilling or derrick or mining or blasting work as the subject matter, and some take on-site assistance and coordination as the subject matter.

Core purpose of this occupation | Taking extraction equipment and machinery and drilling tools and the site and work procedures as the subject matter, complete work within the scope of craft workers and safety and authorization: materials and transport and unloading and organizing, equipment installation and adjustment, observing and monitoring operation, assisting extraction operations, cleaning and preparing the site and records, producing procedure-conforming assisted work and traceable records.

Main subject matter and basis of adjacent positions | Earth drillers rely on drilling processes and geological requirements; derrick operators rely on oil and gas drilling and well control procedures; blasters rely on blasting design and civil explosives codes; mining machine operators rely on mining equipment operating procedures; construction laborers rely on general construction and work procedures. Most of them take independent drilling or derrick or blasting or mining or general construction as the subject matter, which differs from this occupation's on-site extraction coordination.

Main subject matter and basis of this occupation | Taking the site and working face, equipment and machinery and drilling tools, materials and spare parts, key points for observing and monitoring equipment operation, excavation and loading and handling, cleaning and site tidying before and after work, and signals and communication and work permit requirements as the subject matter, complete coordination and judgments according to work procedures and current standards and work safety and special operations and occupational health requirements.

Occupational profile | The Helpers--Extraction Workers on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 47-5081.00 (Helpers--Extraction Workers), and takes on on-site coordination tasks such as materials and observation and monitoring and installation and adjustment and handling and cleaning in the extraction crews of mining and quarrying and oil and gas extraction and geological and construction enterprises; the work is mainly on-site physical and equipment and machinery coordination, accompanied by handling and tidying and cleaning and records and collaboration, often performed amid dust and contaminants and noise and open-pit or underground and various weather conditions, and organized according to production plans and processes.

Core processes of adjacent positions | Earth drillers focus on drilling and sampling; derrick operators focus on drilling and well control and tripping; blasters focus on charging and wiring and detonation; mining machine operators focus on mining machine operation; this occupation focuses on observation and monitoring and handling and installation and tidying and cleaning coordination.

Core processes of this occupation | Accepting the task and checking the site, equipment and machinery inspection, material and spare part transport and organizing, equipment installation and adjustment, observing and monitoring operation and assisting extraction, cleaning and preparing the site and records and handover; each step must be performed according to work procedures and craft worker instructions and be reviewable by craft workers and quality control and safety personnel.

Main outputs of adjacent positions | Earth drillers produce boreholes and core samples and drilling records; derrick operators produce drilling and well control and tripping records; blasters produce blasting work and safety records; mining machine operators produce mining work and equipment operation records; these differ from this occupation's coordination work and equipment and work records.

Main outputs of this occupation | Assisted work completed according to work procedures (transported and unloaded materials and parts, installed and adjusted equipment, observation and monitoring records, assisted extraction work, cleaned and tidied sites), equipment and work and inspection records, material and usage and rework records, anomaly and outstanding item records, and traceable shift and handover records.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions | Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the affiliated enterprise and production and safety and quality systems, and the objects of responsibility are mostly equipment and personal safety and production continuity and the environment.

This occupation is responsible for its own observation and monitoring and handling and installation and adjustment and tidying and cleaning and records, and for the assisted work performed according to work procedures and safety requirements; matters involving blasting and explosives, equipment safety inspection, heights and edges, and major quality and safety matters must be referred to the appropriate position or organization according to qualifications and job authorization and policy.

Authority and approval of adjacent positions | The authority of positions in the same group and adjacent positions comes from enterprise authorization and production and safety and professional specifications, and usually does not include the authority to decide on blasting design or equipment modification or major dispositions; matters involving blasting and equipment modification and special operations and major rework should be transferred to the appropriate position or organization.

Authority and approval of this occupation | Daily observation and monitoring and handling and installation and adjustment and tidying and cleaning must be carried out within the scope of the craft worker and job authorization and work procedures; matters involving blasting and explosives and height and edges and machinery and loading and unloading operations, and equipment modification and major rework must be carried out according to policy and qualifications; matters involving blasting and special operations qualifications and work permits are governed by the requirements of the competent authority and the enterprise.

Conclusion boundaries of adjacent positions | Conclusions of positions in the same group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to this equipment or this process level and usually do not constitute a determination of production safety or project acceptance or legal liability; conclusions that cross disciplines or involve blasting and major safety have limits on their applicability.

Conclusion boundaries of this occupation | Observation and monitoring and installation and adjustment and cleaning conclusions state only verifiable records and work content and results, and distinguish measured facts from judgment inferences and items to be verified; conclusions on matters beyond one's own qualifications (blasting work conclusions, equipment safety inspection conclusions, accident determinations) must not be issued in one's own name.

Pre-onboarding checklist notes | The following six items are used to check off one by one before applying and onboarding, to avoid inferring actual duties and authorization from the job title or promotional language; the check results should be based on written recruitment information and the employment contract and job description and production and safety system documents, and should be continuously confirmed after onboarding. This page only lists checklist points and does not constitute a hiring or safety conclusion.

Checklist point notes | Job titles are similar but duties and authorization differ greatly: some focus on materials and handling and observation, some on equipment installation and adjustment, some on specific sites (open-pit mines or underground or oil and gas sites or geological drilling), and some also cover blasting and loading and unloading and machinery coordination; different enterprises and jurisdictions have different requirements for blasting and special operations and qualifications and safety, so check first and then judge fit.

01 Actual job duties and work and site authority | Check whether you truly take on on-site coordination such as observation and monitoring and handling and installation and adjustment, or mainly cleaning and assistance; check the sites and work types you can take part in (open-pit mines or underground or oil and gas or geological drilling or construction), the authority to use tools and machinery and equipment, the authority to take part in blasting and work permits, and the interface relationships with craft workers and crews and equipment and safety personnel.

Checklist point notes | This occupation often works amid dust and contaminants and noise and open-pit or underground and various weather conditions and involves blasting and machinery risk, and usually requires training in safety and blasting and explosives and machinery and height and edges and occupational health, and compliance with personal protection and emergency response requirements.

02 Safety and occupational health and blasting and machinery and height requirements | Check whether the enterprise requires and provides: safety operating procedures and blasting and explosives and work permit training; machinery and height and edge and loading and unloading operation permit requirements; personal protection and emergency response and drills; requirements for the disposal and reporting of dust and contaminants and wastewater and waste; and requirements for identifying and reporting equipment and site hazards.

BLS Table 1.2 shows about 7,100 jobs in 2025 for U.S. occupation 47-5081 and projects about 7,200 in 2035, a reported change of +1.7%. It projects about 700 openings annually, including replacements. Employment counts are rounded independently.

03 Education and training and on-the-job training and qualification requirements | Check whether vocational school training or on-the-job experience is required (that page's Job Zone 1-2 (little or no preparation needed to some preparation needed) and SVP below 6.0 (SVP Below 6.0)); whether mentor-based training or on-the-job training is provided; whether blasting and special operations and working-at-height and machinery operation qualifications or in-house enterprise training and assessment are required; and whether the training and assessment cover observation and monitoring and installation and adjustment and handling and cleaning and safety and emergency response.

Checklist point notes | This occupation is mainly control and handling and operation and repair and communication (controlling machines and processes 94 and handling and moving objects 94 and operating vehicles 93 and repairing and maintaining mechanical equipment 89 are the highest activities; exposure to hazardous equipment and contaminants and noise is common, decision frequency is high, consequences of error are relatively serious, responsibility for others' health and safety is relatively high, and there are production and process constraints), so the site environment and physical and safety tolerance must be included in the check.

04 Pay, working hours, and employment contract scope | Check the composition of the offered pay (base wage, overtime and shift work and high temperature and field allowances, piece rate and crew performance, differences by region and enterprise and site, social insurance and housing fund and labor protection and protective equipment and board and lodging arrangements), working hours and scheduling and site rotation and winter shutdown arrangements, contract term and probation and termination conditions, and training and qualification and promotion arrangements; the U.S.-scope median and percentiles serve only as market reference and are not equal to the offer of any enterprise or region.

Checklist point notes | The interface relationships with craft workers and crews and production and equipment and safety parties determine the boundaries of observation and installation and adjustment and acceptance and authorization and responsibility and disclosure, and must be clarified in advance.

05 Interfaces with craft workers and crews and projects | Check the authority to confirm and adjust equipment and machinery and work, the arrangements for applying for and using and reviewing tools and spare parts, the path for observation and installation and adjustment and nonconforming or rework items, and the requirements for handling and externally providing enterprise and site and equipment manufacturer technical materials.

Checklist point notes | The traceability and record-keeping requirements for task sheets and equipment and observation and monitoring and materials and usage and anomalies determine quality and responsibility definition, and the specifications for templates and time limits and modification and archiving and authority and retention periods must be clarified in advance (materials involving enterprise and site and equipment manufacturer technical materials must also be managed under confidentiality and minimum necessity requirements).

06 Equipment and operation and cleaning and record requirements | Check the requirements for task sheet records, equipment and machinery and observation and monitoring records, material and usage records, installation and adjustment and assisting extraction records, cleaning and tidying and site restoration records, rework records, anomaly and outstanding item records, and work permits and shift handover and original records and revision trail.

paragraphs: Conclusion | The core difference between this page (O*NET 47-5081.00 Helpers--Extraction Workers) and adjacent positions lies in "subject matter and outputs and authorization level": this occupation takes extraction equipment and machinery and the site and on-site coordination as its subject matter, producing assisted work completed according to work procedures together with traceable equipment and work records; earth drillers and derrick operators and blasters and roustabouts and construction laborers focus on their own subject matter, with different outputs and authorization levels.

Evidence note | The comparison objects in the table below come from the O*NET occupational classification and public materials, and are used to help distinguish the work content of adjacent occupations and choose a fit; they do not constitute qualification, hiring, or pay conclusions, nor safety, blasting, special operations, or legal advice. The wages and employment of each occupation must be checked according to its own occupational code and statistical scope and cannot be applied to one another.

Preface | The following comparison is presented in four columns: "career direction — core work and outputs — key differences — what it suits better". Drilling and derrick and blasting and roustabout and construction positions often connect within the same site and process, but connection does not mean they are interchangeable; each position differs in subject matter, equipment, qualifications, and responsibility boundaries and must be checked separately.

Key difference: this occupation takes extraction equipment and machinery and the site and on-site coordination as its subject matter, completing observation and monitoring and handling and installation and adjustment and cleaning within the scope of craft worker and job authorization based on equipment and site and coordination ability, and is responsible for work safety and production order; adjacent positions take independent drilling or derrick or blasting or roustabout or general construction as their subject matter, with different specialties and authorization.

Better suited to people who are willing to work hands-on around equipment and machinery and the site, can do observation and monitoring and handling and installation and tidying and cleaning solidly according to craft workers and procedures, and take responsibility for work safety and production order.

Core work and outputs: driving mobile equipment to transport materials and parts to the excavation site, using hand tools to unload materials and devices, installing and adjusting excavation equipment, observing and monitoring equipment operation during extraction, and organizing materials and cleaning and preparing the site; the outputs are assisted work completed according to work procedures together with equipment and work records.
This occupation: Helpers--Extraction Workers (O*NET/SOC 47-5081.00, Helpers--Extraction Workers)

Key difference: it takes independent drilling and sampling as the subject matter, producing boreholes and drilling records; this occupation takes on-site coordination as the subject matter, with a different authorization level.

Better suited to people who are willing to engage in earth drilling and sampling; this occupation is more oriented toward on-site coordination of materials and observation and monitoring and installation.
Core work and outputs: taking geological and earth drilling and sampling and wall protection as the subject matter, producing boreholes and core samples and drilling records.
Earth drillers, except oil and gas (Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas, 47-5023.00)

Key difference: it takes oil and gas drilling and well control as the subject matter, producing drilling and tripping records; this occupation takes on-site coordination as the subject matter, with different specialties and authorization.
Better suited to people who are willing to engage in oil and gas drilling and derrick operation; this occupation is more oriented toward coordination of site materials and observation and monitoring.
Core work and outputs: taking oil and gas drilling and well control and tripping operations as the subject matter, producing drilling and well control and tripping records.
Oil and gas derrick operators (Oil and Gas Derrick Operators, 47-5012.00)

Key difference: it takes blasting operations as the subject matter, producing blasting and safety records; this occupation takes on-site coordination as the subject matter and does not bear blasting operation responsibility.
Better suited to people who are willing to engage in blasting operations; this occupation is more oriented toward coordination of site materials and observation and cleaning.
Core work and outputs: taking blasting design and charging and wiring and detonation as the subject matter, producing blasting work and safety records.
Blasters and explosives workers and ordnance handling experts (Blasters and Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters, 47-5032.00)

Key difference: it takes oil and gas site roustabout work as the subject matter, producing site work records; this occupation takes extraction and drilling coordination as the subject matter, with different sites and specialties.
Better suited to people who are willing to engage in oil and gas site roustabout work; this occupation is more oriented toward on-site coordination of extraction and drilling.
Core work and outputs: taking the handling and maintenance and cleaning of oil and gas site equipment and tubular goods as the subject matter, producing site work and equipment records.
Roustabouts, oil and gas (Roustabouts, Oil and Gas, 47-5071.00)

Key difference: it takes general construction and demolition and handling as the subject matter, producing construction work records; this occupation takes extraction and drilling coordination as the subject matter, with a different specialty direction.

Better suited to people who are willing to engage in general construction and demolition and handling; this occupation is more oriented toward material and observation and cleaning coordination for extraction and drilling crews.
Core work and outputs: taking earthwork and demolition and handling and assistance at general construction sites as the subject matter, producing general construction work and safety records.
Construction laborers (Construction Laborers, 47-2061.00)

Transition | This page places adjacent positions side by side by "subject matter and outputs and authorization level" in order to help you judge which kind of drilling or derrick or blasting or roustabout or construction position you want to invest in long term. Whichever direction you choose, what really determines whether you can take the job is the equipment and process and safety and qualification ability of that direction, together with the target enterprise's and jurisdiction's requirements for training and blasting and special operations and qualifications; wages and employment must be checked according to each occupation's own code and statistical scope and cannot be applied to one another.
